q-25070.worked_solution:

q-65381.name: Question 3
q-65381.worked_solution:
Remember that $cot$ is the reciprocal of $tan.$ So first we need to compute tangent:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{PR}{QR}=\frac{3}{QR}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the length $QR,$ we can use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}QR & =\sqrt{P{Q}^{2}-P{R}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3\sqrt{5})^{2}-{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45-9} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{-1}=2.
$$

EXPLANATION

Remember that cot is the reciprocal of tan. So first we need to compute tangent: tan⁡θ=oppositeadjacent=PRQR=3QR

To find the length QR, we can use the Pythagorean Theorem: QR=PQ2−PR2=(35)2−32=45−9=36=6.

So we have tan⁡θ=36=12,

and therefore cot⁡θ=(12)−1=2.

q-122902.name: Question 4
q-122902.worked_solution:
Remember that $csc$ is the reciprocal of $sin.$ So first we need to compute sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡P=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{QR}{PR}=\frac{QR}{15}
$$

To find the length $QR,$ we can use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}QR & =\sqrt{P{R}^{2}-P{Q}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{15}^{2}-{9}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{225-81} \\  & =\sqrt{144} \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

So we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡P=\frac{QR}{15}=\frac{12}{15}=\frac{4}{5},
$$

and therefore

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡P={(\frac{4}{5})}^{-1}=\frac{5}{4}.
$$

Question 4
?

csc⁡P=

a
 157
b
 95
c
 85
d
 125
e
 54
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Remember that csc is the reciprocal of sin. So first we need to compute sine:

sin⁡P=oppositehypotenuse=QRPR=QR15

To find the length QR, we can use the Pythagorean Theorem:

QR=PR2−PQ2=152−92=225−81=144=12

So we have

sin⁡P=QR15=1215=45,

and therefore csc⁡P=(45)−1=54.
